newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus agency changes ratings for S. Korean banks.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus agency changes ratings for S. Korean banks.

text.p: A Cyprus-based bank rating agency on Friday said it was adjusting its ratings for three South Korean banks which have had substantial exposure to the stricken Hanbo group.
Capital Intelligence said it is reducing ratings of the Korea First Bank (KFB) to BBB- long term from BBB+, and A-2 short-term from A-1.
KFB's total exposure to Hanbo and Youone, a construction company acquired by Hanbo in 1995, is 1,704 billion won (US$1.97 billion), Capital Intelligence said.
Hanbo Steel, the nation's second largest steelmaker, defaulted on debt repayments last week after piling up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.

The Bank's aggregate non-performing loans including Hanbo/Youone will amount to 11 percent of total loan portfolio. Additional provisions required for this exposure are likely to result in a net loss in 1997, Capital Intelligence said.
Despite the likelihood of state support for major Korean banks, the further deterioration of KFB's already questionable financial position dictates the ratings adjustment, it said.
The agency added it was maintaining its ratings for Cho Hung Bank (CHB) and Korea Exchange Bank (KEB) at A long-term and A-1 short-term for present, but assigned both a negative outlook.
CHB's aggregate exposure to Hanbo is 494 billion won, while KEB lent a total of 421 billion won. All of CHB's exposure to Hanbo is secured, as is the majority of KEB's.
Capital Intelligence said that it is maintaining its ratings of AA long-term and A-1+ short term for Korea Development Bank (KDB) with a stable outlook.
